title: Responses concordance matrix and gradual-degradation playbook
creator: Marco Reynolds
description: Create a canonical concordance matrix that maps OpenAI Responses API primitives to Redwood's Responses model and identify behavioral deltas that require runtime heuristics or gradual degradation policies. Deliver a playbook for runtime routing, canary rules, and automated fallbacks to minimize customer-visible regressions when serving OpenAI-compatible requests through Redwood's API or translation shim.
background_and_rationale: Customers expect existing integrations built for the OpenAI Responses API to work with Redwood's hosted and private runtimes. We have subtle differences in the event stream envelope, tool-calling lifecycle, and structured output typing that cause edge-case regressions. Rather than a one-to-one shim that attempts perfect parity (which is brittle), we want a documented concordance matrix and a pragmatic set of runtime heuristics that gracefully degrade behavior while preserving safety, latency SLAs, and observability.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical mapping document exists that enumerates OpenAI Responses artifacts (events, fields, error states) and the corresponding Redwood representation or transformation rule.
For each mapped delta, a recommended mitigation is defined: translation rule, runtime heuristic, or explicit 'not supported' response template.
Runtime can apply a three-tier fallback policy: exact mapping -> heuristic translation -> governed degradation, and can be toggled per-customer or per-route.
Integration test harness validates 60+ behavioral scenarios (streaming tokens, function/tool lifecycle, structured output objects, partial responses) against expected outputs.
Console dashboard shows parity score by route/model and emits alerts when regression > X% on production traffic.
Migration notes and client guidance doc published (Confluence + public SDK guidance) explaining known incompatibilities and recommended changes for customers.
No P0 customer-facing regression introduced when the concordance/shim is enabled behind a canary flag for 5 pilot customers.
scope: Inventory all OpenAI Responses events (response.start, response.delta, response.function_call, response.tool_event, response.finish, response.error) and map fields to Redwood's internal events. Call out behavioral differences: chunking semantics, role/name attributes on deltas, embedded tool-call termination criteria, finalization of structured output, and error propagation strategies.
out_of_scope: Full emulation of OpenAI SDK semantics for every historical client-side bug or undocumented behavior. Deep changes to user-facing SDKs (these will be covered in follow-up PM tickets).
decision_log: 2026-02-10: Decided to prefer documented heuristics over brittle parity hacks when behavior is undefined in the OpenAI spec. - Marco R.
2026-02-18: Agreed on three-tier fallback policy and feature-flag gating per-customer route. - Priya K., Liam O'Connor
2026-03-01: Chose to publish mapping as a living Concordance Matrix (CSV + Markdown) and expose parity metrics in Console instead of trying to hide differences. - PM and Design review
tradeoffs: Strict parity increases implementation complexity and test surface area; heuristics may occasionally differ from some client expectations but reduce operational fragility.
Runtime translation adds latency (~5-15ms average) for affected streams; we will only enable heuristics when necessary (canary + per-route opt-in).
Providing explicit 'not supported' early could break clients that depend on lenient behavior; gradual degradation mitigates abrupt failures at cost of increased complexity in correctness proofs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Silent semantic drift causing subtle output quality regressions. Mitigation: parity score + eval prompt suite + rollout gates.
Risk: Tool calling state divergence (double-invoke, truncated args). Mitigation: implement an idempotency token for function invocations and reconcile at finish events.
Risk: Streaming envelope mismatch floods logs and overwhelms parsers. Mitigation: provide a testing mode that emits a normalized stream sample and rate-limits debug logs in production.
implementation_notes: Step 1: Build Concordance Matrix skeleton (CSV rows: openai_event, openai_field, observed_behavior, redwood_transform, mitigation, test_case_id).
Step 2: Instrument runtime to tag incoming OpenAI-compatible requests and route through 'oa-compat' translation layer when enabled.

Step 3: Implement small set of heuristics: (a) delta->role mapping fallback, (b) tool_call finalization on 'finish' if no explicit termination, (c) structured-output schema coercion with safety-first strictness flag.
Step 4: Add idempotency tokens on function/tool calls to prevent duplicates during retries and implement once-only delivery semantics where possible.
Step 5: Add parity metric emission: per-request parity_score and delta_reason list (stored as tags in trace).
Step 6: Wire Console parity dashboard and alert rules; add per-route feature flag UI for enabling heuristics.
test_plan: Unit tests for each translation rule (CSV-driven).

End-to-end harness running recorded OpenAI sessions against Redwood shim and asserting normalized outputs for 60+ scenarios (streaming token boundaries, function call mid-stream, tool events with metadata).
Canary on 5 pilot tenants for two weeks with continuous evaluation against baseline OpenAI behavior; rollback criteria: parity breaches > 7% or user-reported errors increase > 10%.
Load tests to measure added latency and resource impact when shim is enabled at 10k rps.
migration_plan: Publish Concordance Matrix and migration notes to Confluence and link in SDK release notes.
Provide example client-side patches for common incompatibilities (e.g., accept both 'tool_call' and 'function_call' envelopes).
Offer customers a 'compatibility audit' service for Dedicated/Private setups during canary to preflight edge-cases.
metrics_and_observability: Parity score (0-100) per-request, aggregated by route/model/customer.
Count of heuristic translations applied per hour and top-5 translation types.
Rate of tool-call de-dup events and function invocation id conflicts.
Console alert when parity score delta > 5% week-over-week for high-traffic routes.
notes_and_examples: Example delta: OpenAI emits 'response.delta' events without author.role consistently; some clients infer 'assistant' while Redwood includes explicit name attribution. Heuristic: default to 'assistant' but attach 'inferred_role' tag in telemetry.

Example tool call: OpenAI's function_call object may be closed implicitly by a 'response.finish' with no explicit 'function_return'. Redwood runtime historically required explicit termination. Heuristic: synthesize a 'function_return' with an empty payload and mark as 'synthesized' so downstream tooling treats it as incomplete.

Example structured output: OpenAI allows more permissive JSONL objects mid-stream; Redwood enforces schema coercion for private deployments. Playbook entry: if coercion fails, emit a partial object and mark 'coercion_failed' with fallback to raw_text output.
